name: PlexusCore
headline: Describe the data you need. PlexusCore builds the pipeline.
summary: An agentic data engineering platform — ask for a model, metric or pipeline in plain language and the agent builds it, tests it, and ships it through a human review gate.
description: PlexusCore is an agentic data engineering platform. Describe what you need in plain English and the agent explores your warehouse, writes the SQL or dbt, tests it, and ships it through a human review gate — with proof of exactly what it did on every run. It works on top of Snowflake, Databricks, dbt and your Git repo, with no rip-and-replace.

capabilities.title: Model your data
capabilities.body: Generate staging models, dimensional models and star schemas from a sentence. PlexusCore draws the ER diagram — dims, facts and their relationships — then writes the build SQL.

capabilities.title: Move your data
capabilities.body: Connect sources and warehouses and let PlexusCore build and schedule the pipelines. Extract, load and transform — orchestrated and monitored.

capabilities.title: Guard your quality
capabilities.body: Profile tables for nulls, duplicates and freshness, and stand up monitors for the ones that matter — freshness, volume, schema drift and custom SQL assertions.

capabilities.title: Explore and answer
capabilities.body: Ask questions in plain language and get grounded answers from live tables — with the query it ran, not a guess.

capabilities.title: Track lineage and metrics
capabilities.body: See what feeds a table and what depends on it before you change it. Define governed metrics once and reuse them everywhere.

capabilities.title: Ship through Git
capabilities.body: Deploy to Snowflake and Databricks, or push to GitHub with two-way sync. Your warehouse and your repo stay in step.

faqs.q: Does PlexusCore replace my data warehouse or dbt?
faqs.a: No. PlexusCore works on top of what you already run — Snowflake, Databricks, dbt, your Git repo. It builds and operates your pipelines; your data never leaves your warehouse.

faqs.q: Can it make changes on its own?
faqs.a: Only if you let it. By default, changes go through a human approval gate. You set the autonomy level per workspace — from propose-only to fully autonomous.

faqs.q: How do I know what the agent actually did?
faqs.a: Every run produces a verifiable record of the tools it called, the tables it read and the writes it made — and it's marked Verified only when everything checked out.

faqs.q: Which platforms does it generate code for?
faqs.a: The one you're connected to. Ask on a Snowflake connection and you get Snowflake SQL; ask with dbt connected and you get dbt models. It won't hand you code it can't run.
Credentials are encrypted in a secrets vault, access is controlled by role and connection, and every action is audit-logged. PlexusCore operates on your data in place.

problem.heading: Data work is bottlenecked on people, not ideas.
body: Every dashboard, model and metric waits in the same queue: a small team of engineers translating requests into SQL, dbt and pipelines by hand. Analysts wait days for a column. Simple changes turn into tickets. And when something ships, no one can say precisely what ran or whether it was checked.
PlexusCore removes the translation bottleneck without removing the human judgment. The agent does the building; your team does the deciding.

how.heading: Chat in. Reviewed pipeline out.
how.intro: PlexusCore runs a real engineering loop on every request — and shows its work at each step.

steps.title: Ask
steps.body: Describe what you want: “Build a customer revenue model,” “Profile the orders table for quality issues,” “Sync Salesforce into the warehouse nightly.”

steps.title: Plan
steps.body: The agent restates the goal and lays out a step-by-step plan before touching anything. Ambiguous request? It asks one sharp question instead of guessing.

steps.title: Build
steps.body: It inspects your live schema, then writes SQL or dbt in your platform's own dialect — never boilerplate it can't run.

steps.title: Test
steps.body: It runs the code, checks row counts, nulls and freshness, and fixes its own errors before handing anything over.

steps.title: Review
steps.body: Nothing ships silently. Finished work goes to an approvals inbox for a human to approve, edit or reject.

steps.title: Ship
steps.body: On approval, deploy to the warehouse or open a pull request in Git. Every change is versioned and reversible.

how.closing: You stay in the loop at exactly one point — the decision to ship.

capabilities.heading: One platform for the whole data-engineering lifecycle.

differentiators.heading: Autonomy you can audit.
differentiators.body: Most AI tools ask you to trust the output. PlexusCore gives you the receipts. Every run produces a proof-of-work record — which tools it called, which tables it read, which writes it made, and whether they passed. A run is only marked Verified when nothing failed and every write went through the approval gate. If the agent couldn't finish, it says so plainly instead of pretending it did.

differentiators.heading: The agent proposes. Your team disposes.
differentiators.body: PlexusCore is built so nothing reaches production unreviewed. Writes to your warehouse, dbt mutations and pipeline runs are governed by policy: in suggest-only mode the agent proposes and stops; in approval mode changes wait in an inbox for a human decision; only in fully autonomous mode does it act on its own — and even then, every action is logged. You choose how much rope to give it, per workspace.

differentiators.heading: It gets better at your data every week.
differentiators.body: When PlexusCore solves a task well, it can save the recipe as a reusable skill. Skills that succeed repeatedly — with no failures — earn certification, and certified skills replay deterministically: the same request returns the same result, without re-invoking the model. Your platform accumulates a library of proven, repeatable operations tuned to your warehouse — not generic prompts.

integrations.heading: Connect what you already run.
integrations.intro: PlexusCore speaks to your stack directly — no rip-and-replace.

groups.label: Sources
groups.items: 600+ connectors, from SaaS apps to databases to object storage

integrations.footnote: Don't see yours? Talk to us — the connector catalog is growing.

security.heading: Enterprise-ready from day one.
security.intro: PlexusCore is built for teams that answer to security and compliance, not just deadlines.

items.label: Access
items.body: SSO via OIDC, role-based access control and SCIM user provisioning.

items.label: Identity
items.body: Multi-factor authentication and per-connection access controls.

items.label: Secrets
items.body: Credentials stored in a secrets vault, encrypted at rest — never in plain text.

items.label: Audit
items.body: A complete, exportable audit trail of every action, human or agent.

items.label: Control
items.body: Policy-gated writes and a human approval inbox on every change.

security.closing: Your data stays in your warehouse. PlexusCore operates on it — it doesn't take custody of it.

audiences.heading: Built for the people who move data.

items.body: Offload the repetitive build work — staging models, tests, backfills — and spend your time on architecture, not tickets.
Turn a request into a reviewed dbt model in minutes, with lineage and tests included.
Cut the backlog and get governance you can prove, without adding headcount.
Ask for the table or metric you need in plain language, and get an answer grounded in real data.

pilot.heading: Start with a guided pilot.
pilot.body: See PlexusCore build a real pipeline against your own warehouse, in a working session with our team. No rip-and-replace, no long setup.

finalCta.heading: Give your data team an agent that ships.
finalCta.subhead: See PlexusCore turn a plain-English request into a reviewed, production-ready pipeline — against your own data.

name: PlexusIQ
headline: From metrics to decisions in one governed layer
summary: A decision-intelligence suite that unifies metrics, ML predictions and natural-language analytics on top of your data platform.
description: PlexusIQ gives your organization a single semantic layer where every metric is defined once and used everywhere — in dashboards, forecasts and conversational analytics. Business users ask questions in plain language; PlexusIQ answers with governed, explainable numbers backed by lineage you can audit.

capabilities.title: Semantic metrics layer
capabilities.body: Version-controlled metric definitions consumed consistently by BI tools, notebooks, APIs and AI assistants.

capabilities.title: Conversational analytics
capabilities.body: Natural-language questions answered from governed metrics — with the SQL, lineage and confidence shown, not hidden.

capabilities.title: Forecasting & ML
capabilities.body: Built-in forecasting, anomaly detection and propensity models that publish predictions back into the metrics layer.

capabilities.title: Decision workflows
capabilities.body: Alerts, approvals and scenario planning that connect insight to the operational systems where decisions execute.

stats.label: Definition per metric, everywhere it is consumed
Of routine reporting questions self-served by business users

faqs.q: Does PlexusIQ replace our BI tools?
faqs.a: No — it feeds them. The semantic layer serves the same governed metrics to your existing BI, notebooks, APIs and the built-in conversational analytics, so adoption starts from the tools people already use.

faqs.q: How does conversational analytics stay trustworthy?
faqs.a: Every answer shows its work: the metric definition used, the generated SQL, the lineage and a confidence signal. Analysts can verify in one click, which is why finance teams sign off on it.
A metrics discovery sprint with your analysts, then the semantic layer built over your existing platform — most clients see their first governed metrics live inside four weeks.

name: AgentMesh
headline: Run AI agents you can actually trust
summary: An orchestration and governance runtime for deploying fleets of AI agents with policy guardrails, observability and human oversight.
description: AgentMesh is the control plane for the agentic enterprise. It lets teams compose agents from models, tools and knowledge; enforces declarative policies on every action; and records complete decision traces. Graduated autonomy means agents earn independence with evidence — and every irreversible action keeps a human hand on the switch.

capabilities.title: Agent orchestration
capabilities.body: Compose single agents or multi-agent workflows with tool access, memory and structured handoffs between agents and humans.

capabilities.title: Policy guardrails
capabilities.body: Declarative rules evaluated on every tool call: permissions, budgets, rate limits and hard stops for irreversible operations.

capabilities.title: Full observability
capabilities.body: Complete traces of inputs, reasoning, actions and outcomes — searchable, auditable and wired to your monitoring stack.

capabilities.title: Evaluation harness
capabilities.body: Continuous regression suites and model-graded scoring so every prompt, model or tool change is proven before release.

stats.label: Of agent actions policy-checked and logged
Average reduction in manual effort on automated workflows

faqs.q: Which model providers does AgentMesh support?
faqs.a: All major providers — Anthropic, OpenAI, the cloud model platforms — plus private deployments. Policy, logging and evaluation sit above the model layer, so you can switch or mix providers without rebuilding governance.

faqs.q: How does AgentMesh satisfy risk and compliance teams?
faqs.a: Declarative policy rules the second line can read and version, complete decision logs retained as a book of record, graduated autonomy with measured reliability, and hard stops on irreversible actions. It was designed with bank validators in the room.

That is the intended path: one workflow, propose-only mode, four to six weeks to a measured baseline — then autonomy expands with evidence. The platform grows from one agent to a governed fleet without re-architecture.
